title: IG2: Risk Assessment (Practical Assessment)
learningObjectives: Understand the IG2 assessment format and marking criteria
Conduct a workplace risk assessment suitable for submission
Write clear, specific hazard and control descriptions that score marks
Complete all required sections of the IG2 observation sheet

content.text: IG2 is the practical component of the NEBOSH IGC. Instead of a written exam, you conduct a real workplace risk assessment and submit a completed observation sheet to NEBOSH. You can choose any workplace — your current employer, a site visit, or a simulated environment. There is no time limit, but NEBOSH expects the assessment to represent approximately 3–4 hours of observation time.

rows: Brief description; helps assessor understand context
Hazard observations with likelihood, severity, risk score, existing controls, and recommended actions
Sufficient breadth and depth of observations

content.text: What NEBOSH Expects in Each Observation Row
Each row on the observation sheet requires five elements. Many candidates lose marks by being vague — be specific.

rows: Specific hazard identified — not just a broad category
Trailing electrical cable from floor-standing fan across main pedestrian walkway
Maintenance workers and office staff — trip, fall, and potential electric shock
3 — Cable is in a high-traffic area and is frequently walked over
4 — Fall could result in fractures or head injury on hard floor
What controls are already in place
Cable has been taped to floor in one section; 'mind the step' sign at entrance
Re-route cable through wall conduit or overhead; add physical barrier if re-routing not possible; review within 2 weeks

content.text: Aim for at least 20 meaningful observations across a range of hazard types. Weak candidates submit 8–10 vague observations. Strong candidates submit 25+ specific observations covering physical, chemical, ergonomic, fire, and psychosocial hazards.
Part 3: Summary of Key Findings — How to Score Well
Part 3 is worth 20 marks and tests your ability to prioritise and justify recommendations. NEBOSH expects you to:

items: Identify the 3–5 highest-priority hazards from your observation sheet
Explain WHY each is a priority (high risk rating, legal requirement, potential for serious harm)
Reference appropriate standards or regulations where relevant
Use professional, report-style language — not bullet points alone
Physical — slip/trip hazards, working at height, noise, temperature, manual handling
Chemical — cleaning chemicals, fuel, dust, fumes (welding, vehicle exhaust)
Fire — ignition sources, housekeeping, exit routes, extinguisher access
Electrical — portable equipment condition, overloaded sockets, cable management
Ergonomic — workstation setup, manual handling tasks, repetitive work
Welfare — welfare facilities, first aid provision, emergency procedures
Workplace transport — vehicles, pedestrian routes, visibility

content.text: NEBOSH allows IG2 to be conducted in any workplace globally, including Gulf O&G sites. If conducting your IG2 on a Gulf site, include Gulf-specific hazards: heat stress controls, H2S detection, PTW compliance, and sun protection measures. These demonstrate additional depth of knowledge and can strengthen your Part 3 summary.

Part 3 Priority Hazard Example: 'The most significant hazard observed was inadequate fall protection on the mezzanine floor storage area. Workers were observed accessing storage at heights of approximately 3.5m without edge protection or fall arrest systems. The risk rating was 5 × 4 = 20 (Critical). Falls from height are the leading cause of fatalities in this industry sector. Immediate action required: prohibit mezzanine access until a suitable edge protection system is installed and a working-at-height risk assessment is completed. Recommended timeframe: within 48 hours.'
